newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman sees few competitors for Wascana.
newsitem.headline: Talisman sees few competitors for Wascana.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc chief executive Jim Buckee said on Thursday he expected few companies could compete with Talisman for Wascana Energy Inc.

Buckee said Talisman was one of a "very limited" list of potential Wascana acquisitors because of the deal's size, the two firms' extensive operational overlap and the need for a bid to be acceptable to the Saskatchewan government.
"I think on these three counts that in fact there will be very limited competition," he told a conference call.

Talisman said on Wednesday it planned to make a C$1.7 billion cash-and-stock takeover offer for Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana. Talisman said it would offer C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of one of its shares for each share of Wascana, a former Saskatchewan government-owned oil company.
It said 40 percent of Wascana shares would be purchased using cash and the rest swapped for Talisman stock. Talisman would also assume about C$200 million in long-term debt.
The cash portion of the deal would total C$615 million and initially be funded by bank debt, which would be cut later by asset sales, Talisman said.
Buckee said that would be reduced after the deal was competed using proceeds from asset sales, which he estimated at C$350 million to C$500 million.
If the deal was made effective as planned on April 1, Talisman's expected 1997 cash flow per share would increase by 10-15 percent, he said.

The acquisition would double its landholdings in western Canada and increase its 1997 oil and gas production by 30 percent to 175,000 barrels per day of oil and 826 million cubic feet per day of natural gas.
Buckee said that he anticipated that Wascana's board would recommend its offer to shareholders. Wascana has yet to reply publicly to Talisman's intentions.

Talisman said it had extensive discussions with the government of Saskatchewan over legislation that requires Wascana's head office to remain in the province, and planned to bring the firm under its wing as a wholly owned subsidiary while keeping its headquarters there for at least five years.
Company officials on Thursday said that the government -- which owns 7.3 million Wascana shares -- has said that Talisman's plans would meet the regulations.
In the conference call, Buckee outlined how Talisman would add to the Regina office by bringing in technical staff to oversee the company's heavy oil operations.
He said that most operations of Wascana are currently run from the Calgary office and only Regina housed only adminstration and executive staff.
Buckee also said that the acquisition would increase its stakes in main operating regions and increase its reserve life and inventory of drilling prospects with little financial strain.
"It's very easily accommodated and of all the companies, this is the best fit for us. There are not many people who can manage an acquisition of this size and operate it easily," he said.
